description: Summarize progress as totals and trends, with no per-design rows: rounds used, hits, best affinity, the cumulative hit curve, hit rate by design class, and predicted against realized rates. Use it for a status review; per-design outcomes are in get_history, budget and rounds in describe_campaign.
name: campaign_summary

description: Summarize each column over the whole pool (min, median, max, share missing and higher_is_better; counts for classes). higher_is_better says which direction is the good one, since values are raw; use it to pick thresholds before querying. It says nothing about which designs are hits.
name: column_summary

description: Show the campaign's state: budget, rounds left, batch size, counts of purchased and pending designs, hits found, and the columns you can query. Call it first and after every submit. It never shows outcomes of designs you have not bought.
name: describe_campaign

description: Estimate the hit rate so far with a 90% interval, optionally per design class, or predict the rate of a proposed next batch. Use it to decide whether more purchases are worthwhile. Next-batch predictions are flagged uncalibrated until 3 rounds of predictions are realized.
name: estimate_hit_rate

description: Fit a regularized logistic model on delivered designs and rank unpurchased designs by predicted hit probability. Needs at least 2 hits and 8 delivered purchases, otherwise it returns insufficient_data. Use it to see which features matter: each weight is in the raw-value direction, so positive means a higher raw value of that column goes with binding.
name: fit_and_rank

description:
Fit your own logistic regression on the delivered results, with the options below, and rank the unpurchased designs; each reported weight is in the raw-value direction, so positive means a higher raw value goes with binding. It needs at least 2 hits and 8 delivered purchases, otherwise it returns insufficient_data; with the default options it is the same model as fit_and_rank. validation compares the model's leave-one-out log loss with a base-rate baseline (improvement above 0 means better than the baseline; compare it with improvement_se) and gives the leave-one-out AUC with its standard error.
Options:
- features: the predicted-score features to use (default: all); length and design class are always inputs.
- scaling: pool standardizes each input with the mean and standard deviation of the whole pool; purchased, with those of your delivered designs.
- penalty and C: l2 shrinks every weight toward zero, l1 can set weights to exactly zero; a smaller C shrinks more (0.001 to 100).
- similarity_feature: adds each design's largest 3-mer sequence similarity to one of your hits as an input (a design is never compared with itself).
- rank_by: mean ranks by predicted hit probability; upper by an optimistic bound, sigmoid(log-odds + kappa x sd), from the model's uncertainty (l2 only; kappa 0 to 5).
- top_k: how many designs to return (at most 50).

C.description: Inverse regularization strength, 0.001 to 100; smaller shrinks more.
C.title: C

features.description: Predicted-score features to use; omit for all of them.
features.title: Features

kappa.description: Width of the optimistic bound in posterior sds, 0 to 5.
kappa.title: Kappa

penalty.description: l2 shrinks all weights; l1 can zero some.
penalty.title: Penalty

rank_by.description: Rank by predicted probability, or by the optimistic bound (l2 only).
rank_by.title: Rank By

scaling.description: Standardize the inputs over the whole pool or your delivered designs.
scaling.title: Scaling

similarity_feature.description: Add each design's largest 3-mer similarity to a hit as an input.
similarity_feature.title: Similarity Feature

top_k.description: How many ranked designs to return, 1 to 50.
top_k.title: Top K

name: fit_custom_model

description: Return one row per delivered purchase, with its features and outcome. Use it to study which of your designs hit and why. Pending designs are not listed.
name: get_history

description: List batches that were submitted but whose results have not arrived; this happens only in games with a result delay. It does not advance time.
name: pending_batches

description:
Run a pre-registered scripted policy on your data so far and get the batch it would buy, with reasons. It spends nothing: to buy the batch, pass its design_ids to submit_batch. Until a model can be fitted (at least 2 hits and 8 delivered purchases), the model-based policies rank by a preset feature instead.
Policies:
- learner: fits a model on your delivered results and ranks the pool by it, plus random exploration.
- learner_sim: like learner, and also ranks by sequence similarity to your hits.
- learner_purchased: like learner, but standardizes the features on your purchased designs, not the whole pool.
- learner_sim_purchased: like learner_sim, but standardizes the features on your purchased designs, not the whole pool.
- random: a uniformly random batch of unpurchased designs.
- fixed: the top unpurchased designs by one feature, given as feature.

exploration.description: Share of the batch, 0 to 1, that the model-based policies pick at random instead of by rank.
exploration.title: Exploration

feature.description: The feature to rank by; only with policy fixed, and required there.
feature.title: Feature

k.description: How many designs to propose, from 1 to the batch size.
k.title: K

policy.description: The scripted policy to run (see the tool description).
policy.title: Policy

name: propose_batch

description: List unpurchased designs with their raw metric values, optionally filtered and sorted (at most 50 rows). Use it to look at candidates before buying, or pass design_ids to look up specific designs (purchased ones included). Values are raw and never reoriented, so for some columns a LOWER value is better and sorting descending returns the worst designs: check the column's higher_is_better, which describe_campaign and column_summary report.
name: query_pool

description: Find unpurchased designs whose sequences are most similar (3-mer cosine) to the designs you give, typically hits. Use it to follow up on a hit. Similarity partly reflects shared authorship, so do not over-buy one family.
name: similar_designs

description: End the campaign with a reason; no further batches can be submitted. Use it when more purchases are unlikely to pay off. It cannot be undone, but pending results can still arrive.
name: stop

description: Report the hit-rate trend and whether the low_yield or decay stop rules have fired. Use it before deciding to stop. The decay rule is noisy and often fires by chance, so treat it as weak evidence.
name: stop_advice

description: Buy up to batch_size designs that are not yet purchased or pending, within budget. Results come back immediately when there is no delay, otherwise through wait or later submits. Do not use it to explore: every call spends a round.
name: submit_batch

description: Advance one round without buying and return any results that arrive. Use it only when something is pending. It fails if nothing is pending.
name: wait
